title: Amended again and again, never rebid
question: Which agreements has the Board amended in three or more different years, extending or raising the same agreement instead of approving a new one?
finding: Of 708 agreements with outside parties that the Board amended at least once from 2014 to 2026, 19 were amended in three or more different years; their latest approved ceilings add up to $1.90 billion. 13 of the 19 were amended in at least half the years between their first and latest Board file. The longest runs: CCT Technologies, Inc. with Office of Contract Administration (4 amendments in 4 years, 2019–2023, $20.0 million to $66.5 million); DFS Group, L.P. with Airport (5 amendments in 4 years, 2018–2025); Xtech JV with Office of Contract Administration (3 amendments in 3 years, 2016–2018, $32.0 million to $109.0 million); Golden Gate Petroleum with Office of Contract Administration (3 amendments in 3 years, 2022–2024, $45.0 million to $102.3 million). Where the contract table holds an agreement of the same size for the same party, 4 are keyed as competed and 2 under a rule that sets competition aside.
how: Board of Supervisors titles were linked into chains for one agreement. As in the amendment-growth screen, only links proven by a dollar figure carried from one title to the next, or by a shared contract number, are followed; grant acceptances, settlements and agreements with other public bodies are left out. A chain is listed when its amendments were introduced in three or more different calendar years. "Share of years" is amendment years divided by the years from the first to the latest file. The rule shown is the purchasing rule keyed on the contract in the Supplier Contracts table whose agreed amount is within 2% of the chain’s latest ceiling for the same party; blank means no such contract was found. Ranked by amendment years.
limits: An amendment is a way to extend or enlarge an agreement, and each one here was put to a public vote. Long agreements for buses, software, fuel, treatment programmes and airport services may be written with options to extend, and an agreement first let by competition and then extended is not a contract that escaped competition. Only amendments that needed a Board vote appear, so smaller agreements amended many times by a department alone are missing. Titles are text-mined; each row links to the latest file. What would settle a row: the original solicitation and its stated term and options, against the dates the amendments extended it to. The paid column counts payments issued in fiscal 2019 to 2026, which is read from the voucher number and not from the year the file lists a line under; $992.6 million of outside spending that the file lists under those years was issued earlier and is left out. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
